text:
A: Hello! Can you hear me alright? There we go. Gareth, is it?
B: Yeah. Hi. I can hear you fine.
A: Lovely. I'm Darren. I've got to say, I clocked that scarf on your wall in the photo. Saints fan?
B: Er, yeah. Since I was a kid. Season ticket, though I only make about half the games.
A: No way. Me too, well, not a season ticket, I'm more of a pub man, but I get down St Mary's a few times a season with a mate. Saturday though, eh? Rubbish.
B: Yeah, that was poor. No shape in the second half at all.
A: None. I was sat in the Red Lion shouting at the telly like it was gonna help. Anyway, yeah. Where are you, then?
B: Andover. Grew up in Basingstoke though.
A: Get out. I'm Basingstoke, born and bred, still here. Which school?
B: Er, I went to the sixth-form college after. You'd probably know it.
A: Oh yeah, I know it. I didn't last that long, me, I was out at sixteen and on a trade counter. Builders' merchants. Been there over twenty years now, I'm branch manager, so it's timber, plumbing, heavy-side, all that, about fourteen staff. And you?
B: Warehousing and distribution. Three sites along the M3 and the A303. I'm operations director.
A: Director, very nice. So you'll know the M3 roadworks, then.
B: Every morning. I'm in early for the handover, so I miss the worst of it, but the way back's grim.
A: It's a nightmare, mate. I sat on it Tuesday for forty minutes. Got done by a speed camera on the A33 the week before, as well, so I'm not having much luck with roads at the minute. Company car, so I sort of tell myself it's not my petrol, you know, but the points are still mine.
B: Yeah. That's the bit that matters.
A: Do you get a car with yours?
B: Er, I do, yeah. They offered me an upgrade last year, but we had a pay freeze on, so I said no. Didn't look right.
A: Fair play. I don't think I'd have the willpower, honestly. I'm already browsing what I'm getting next, I'm looking at the new A5. Nicola thinks I'm sad.
B: Each to their own.
A: Ha, that's diplomatic. Kids?
B: Two. Josh is sixteen, doing his GCSEs. Ellie's nineteen, she's at uni in Southampton.
A: You're joking. My daughter's Ellie, she's sixteen, mocks coming up. And my lad's at uni, Nottingham. It's like looking in a mirror, this. Do you find it quiet with one gone?
B: Er, yeah. Bit. You notice it at dinner, sort of thing. One less plate.
A: Yeah, yeah. We've got the dog, Murphy, so he fills the gap. Ate a tea towel last week, an entire tea towel, cost us two hundred quid at the vet. Have you got a dog?
B: Not anymore. Ours died a couple of years ago. Haven't got round to another one.
A: Ah, sorry, mate. Anyway, that puzzle at the start, did you finish it? I gave up and guessed half of it.
B: I finished it. Took me a while. The last couple I wasn't sure about.
A: You're more patient than me. I'm learn-on-the-job, me, I'm no good with things on paper. That's why I've got an assistant manager who does all my rotas.
B: Rotas I can do. Hundred and eighty staff, we're trialling a new shift pattern at the minute, it's eating my week.
A: Hundred and eighty! Blimey. See, you'd want a pint after that. Do you play golf at all?
B: No. I run, mostly. Before work.
A: Running. Yeah, I'm more of a nineteenth-hole man, to be honest. I play once a month, badly, and then the bar's the best bit.
B: Sounds about right for most golfers.
A: Ha! Exactly. Here, we should get a—
